22	 * Signals that a request the controller has begun to process must be rejected with a specific
23	 * client-error {@link HttpStatus} — {@code 400 Bad Request}, {@code 409 Conflict} or
24	 * {@code 429 Too Many Requests}. Request handling throws this instead of building a rejection
25	 * response itself, so the single translation from a rejection to its HTTP response lives in
26	 * {@link ExceptionControllerAdvice#handleRejectedRequestException}, alongside the other
27	 * exception-to-response mappings.
28	 */

34	        this.status = status;

content.text:
Build is green. Let me confirm the full picture is consistent — all four RFC7807 members are present for every rejection path.

The change is complete and the test suite passes (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

## What I did

The gap was in `ExceptionControllerAdvice.handleRejectedRequestException` — the handler for `RejectedRequestException`, which is the exception the owner-create flow throws for all the business-rule rejections (400 Bad Request, 409 Conflict, 429 Too Many Requests). It was returning:

```java
return ResponseEntity.status(status).build();   // status only, empty body
```

That produced the correct HTTP status but no body at all — violating the spec's requirement that 400/409/429 rejections carry an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body.

I changed it to build a `ProblemDetail` via the existing `detailBuild(...)` helper (the same one the other handlers use), so the response now carries all four required members:

- `type` — the request URL
- `title` — the exception class name
- `status` — set by `ProblemDetail.forStatus(status)`, equal to the HTTP status
- `detail` — the status reason phrase

```java
HttpStatus status = e.getStatus();
logger.warn("Request rejected at {} {} with status {}",
    request.getMethod(), request.getRequestURI(), status.value());
ProblemDetail detail = this.detailBuild(e, status, request.getRequestURL(), status.getReasonPhrase());
return ResponseEntity.status(status).body(detail);
```

- `title` — the exception class name

return ResponseEntity.status(status).body(detail);
